quests.instruction: What is the action word for using colorful liquid and a brush to make art?
quests.hint: Think about what you do with a brush and colorful paint.
quests.explanation: Paint means to use color and a brush to make art. We paint pictures at school!
quests.funFact: Long ago, people painted pictures on cave walls to tell stories!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for using scissors to separate paper into pieces?
quests.hint: Think about what you do to paper with a pair of scissors.
quests.explanation: Cut means to use something sharp, like scissors, to separate things. We cut paper for crafts!
quests.funFact: Learning to cut carefully with scissors is an important school skill!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for using your hands and feet to go up something high?
quests.hint: Think about what you do on a ladder or a big tree.
quests.explanation: Climb means to use your hands and feet to go up. We climb ladders and playground bars!
quests.funFact: Climbing makes your arms and legs strong at the same time!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for moving on your hands and knees close to the ground?
quests.hint: Think about how a baby moves before they can walk.
quests.explanation: Crawl means to move on your hands and knees. Babies crawl before they learn to walk!
quests.funFact: Crawling helps babies grow strong muscles for walking later!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for making a small jump, often on just one foot?
quests.hint: Think about how a bunny moves across the grass.
quests.explanation: Hop means to make a small jump, sometimes on one foot. Bunnies love to hop!
quests.funFact: Rabbits and frogs are both champion hoppers!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for moving forward with a little hop after every step?
quests.hint: Think about a happy, bouncy way of walking to the park.
quests.explanation: Skip means to move forward with a small hop between steps. We skip when we feel happy!
quests.funFact: Skipping uses both sides of your body working together!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for sitting on something and moving, like on a bike?
quests.hint: Think about what you do when you sit on your bicycle and pedal.
quests.explanation: Ride means to travel by sitting on or in something, like a bike. We ride bikes outside!
quests.funFact: Riding a bicycle is a fun way to exercise and explore your neighborhood!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for moving through the air, like a bird or an airplane?
quests.hint: Think about how a bird moves from tree to tree.
quests.explanation: Fly means to move through the air. Birds and airplanes both fly!
quests.funFact: Birds have light, hollow bones that help them fly high in the sky!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for making food ready to eat, often using heat?
quests.hint: Think about what a chef does in the kitchen before dinner.
quests.explanation: Cook means to make food ready to eat, often with heat. We cook yummy meals together!
quests.funFact: Cooking food can make it taste better and safer to eat!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for tipping a liquid out of a container?
quests.hint: Think about what you do with a jug to fill up your cup.
quests.explanation: Pour means to tip a liquid so it flows out. We pour milk into a cup!
quests.funFact: Pouring carefully helps keep the table nice and dry!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for paying attention to a sound with your ears?
quests.hint: Think about what you do with your ears during story time.
quests.explanation: Listen means to pay attention with your ears. We listen to music and stories!
quests.funFact: Listening carefully helps you learn new things every day!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for using your eyes to see something?
quests.hint: Think about what you do with your eyes to find your toy.
quests.explanation: Look means to use your eyes to see something. We look both ways before crossing!
quests.funFact: Your eyes can see thousands of different colors!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for using your finger to show where something is?
quests.hint: Think about what you do with your finger to show a friend something exciting.
quests.explanation: Point means to use your finger to show where something is. We point to show the way!
quests.funFact: Pointing is a way people can communicate without using any words at all!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for moving your head up and down to say yes?
quests.hint: Think about how you move your head when you agree with someone.
quests.explanation: Nod means to move your head up and down, usually to say yes. We nod when we agree!
quests.funFact: A nod is understood as yes in many countries around the world!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for closing just one eye quickly and playfully?
quests.hint: Think about closing only one eye to share a fun, friendly secret.
quests.explanation: Wink means to close just one eye quickly. We wink to share a friendly, funny moment!
quests.funFact: Winking uses tiny muscles that you can control all by yourself!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for quickly closing and opening both your eyes?
quests.hint: Think about what your eyes do all by themselves, again and again.
quests.explanation: Blink means to quickly close and open both eyes. We blink to keep our eyes clean!
quests.funFact: You blink about once every few seconds without even thinking about it!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for using your hand to feel something?
quests.hint: Think about what you do with your fingers to feel if something is soft.
quests.explanation: Touch means to use your hand or fingers to feel something. We touch soft blankets!
quests.funFact: Your fingertips are one of the most sensitive parts of your whole body!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for using your nose to notice a scent?
quests.hint: Think about what you do with your nose near a fresh flower.
quests.explanation: Smell means to use your nose to notice a scent. We smell yummy cookies baking!
quests.funFact: Your nose can notice thousands of different smells!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for using your tongue to notice a flavor?
quests.hint: Think about what you do with your tongue when you try new food.
quests.explanation: Taste means to use your tongue to notice a flavor. We taste sweet and sour foods!
quests.funFact: Your tongue can notice flavors like sweet, sour, and salty!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for holding something and moving it with you?
quests.hint: Think about what you do with your backpack on the way to school.
quests.explanation: Carry means to hold something while you move it. We carry our backpacks to school!
quests.funFact: Ants can carry things that are many times heavier than their own body!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for using your arms to raise something up?
quests.hint: Think about what you do with a toy box to move it off the floor.
quests.explanation: Lift means to use your strength to raise something up. We lift toys off the ground!
quests.funFact: Lifting things safely helps keep your muscles strong!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for letting go of something so it falls down?
quests.hint: Think about what happens if you open your hand and let a ball go.
quests.explanation: Drop means to let something fall by letting go of it. We drop a ball to bounce it!
quests.funFact: Everything that drops falls down to the ground because of gravity!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for a ball hitting the ground and popping back up?
quests.hint: Think about what a basketball does when a player pats it on the floor.
quests.explanation: Bounce means to spring back up after hitting a surface. A ball can bounce many times!
quests.funFact: A bouncy ball is full of air, which helps it bounce so high!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for something turning over and over as it moves?
quests.hint: Think about what a ball does when you push it along the ground.
quests.explanation: Roll means to move by turning over and over. We roll a ball across the floor!
quests.funFact: Round things like balls and wheels are perfect shapes for rolling!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for turning around and around in one spot?
quests.hint: Think about what a top does when you twist it and let go.
quests.explanation: Spin means to turn around and around quickly. A top can spin for a long time!
quests.funFact: The Earth is always spinning, even though we cannot feel it!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for moving something quickly side to side or up and down?
quests.hint: Think about what you do to a bottle to mix up the juice inside.
quests.explanation: Shake means to move something quickly back and forth. We shake a bottle to mix it up!
quests.funFact: Shaking hands is a friendly way people say hello!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for bending down so your knees touch the ground?
quests.hint: Think about what you do to get down to a puppy's height.
quests.explanation: Kneel means to bend down so your knees rest on the ground. We kneel to look at small things!
quests.funFact: Kneeling down is a comfy way to talk to someone shorter than you!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for reaching your arms and legs out to make your body long?
quests.hint: Think about what you do with your arms right after you wake up.
quests.explanation: Stretch means to reach your body out long. We stretch to wake up our muscles!
quests.funFact: Stretching in the morning can help your body feel ready for the day!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for opening your mouth wide when you feel sleepy?
quests.hint: Think about what your mouth does when you feel very tired.
quests.explanation: Yawn means to open your mouth wide when you are tired. We yawn before bedtime!
quests.funFact: Seeing someone yawn might make you feel like yawning too!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for opening your eyes and stopping sleep in the morning?
quests.hint: Think about what you do when the morning sun comes up.
quests.explanation: Wake means to stop sleeping and open your eyes. We wake up every morning!
quests.funFact: Waking up at the same time every day helps your body feel its best!
